tax_exemption: Charitable-society income is statutorily exempt under the Income Tax Act (Cap. 123) if applied to charitable purposes - no separate tax application; donations to charities are not deductible; timing unpublished.

A company or irrevocable trust applies to the tax Commissioner under the Income Tax Act 2023; approved non-profits have exempt income; donations to them are deductible; no VAT relief; timing unpublished.

Separate certification by the Finance Secretary under Business Tax Act 2016 s.6 (charitable/educational/sporting/religious purpose, no profit split); certified non-profits are exempt from business tax.

Charitable and benevolent organisation income is exempt under the Income Tax Act 1992 exempt-income schedule (purposive test, no separate tax application); no donor-deduction regime and no VAT; time unpublished.
Not automatic: the Non-Profit Entities Act 2020 requires a non-profit to apply to the Department of Revenue for exemption from the 3% Net Profit Tax; no donor-deduction regime; timing unpublished.

No separate charitable exemption: FSM corporate income tax hits only 'major corporations' ($1M+ equity), so a small non-profit is out of scope; state-level taxes may apply; no donor deduction; timing unpublished.

Vakif registered with the Foundations Affairs Presidency; foundations are exempt from corporate tax on charitable income; donors deduct gifts up to 10% of taxable profit (uncapped for listed); no VAT exemption.

Charitable status confirmed by the State Tax Service (charitable purpose, no profit distribution); charitable income exempt; donors deduct gifts up to 10% of taxable income (art. 117); 1-month decision.
NPOs registered with the Justice Ministry; donations and goods for charity are VAT-exempt and charitable activity is profit-tax-privileged; donor deduction capped at 0.25% of taxable profit.
No automatic income-tax exemption: NCOs pay 20% profit tax; Tax Code art. 106.1.18 adds a limited donor deduction for supporting social-purpose foundations (2023); no VAT exemption.

NPOs registered with the Justice Committee under the Tax Code's NPO regime: charitable contributions received are not income and charitable operations are VAT-exempt; donors get a limited deduction (2022).
Registered with the Justice Ministry; 'charitable organization' status itself gives no special benefit - registered NNOs are generally income-tax exempt on non-commercial charitable income.
Associations need Justice Ministry consent plus state registration; a charity foundation can only be created by government decree (5+ citizen founders); law provides tax benefits, detail sparse.
Public associations registered with the Justice Ministry; NPO income from charitable activity and donations is income-tax exempt under the Tax Code (2023 NCO tax guide); no donor deduction.

Charitable funds registered with the State Registration Service; tax status requires charitable purpose and no profit split; charity profits are income-tax exempt (Tax Code art. 212); no donor deduction.
Registered NGOs (Interior Ministry) are exempt on donations, gifts and membership fees under Direct Taxation Act art. 139 if used for charter purposes per National Tax Administration approval.

Association declared with the Interior Ministry; ONG status needs a separate 'agrement'; recognised ONGs are exempt from income tax, registration duties and VAT (Law 99/014 art. 18); no donor-deduction regime.
Association declared under the civil code; ONG status requires the state's administrative 'agrement' (ONG law) to act nationally; the CGI grants limited exemptions to recognised ONGs; detail sparse.

Association registered with the Interior Ministry (Ordinance 023/PR/2018); international NGOs need extra authorisation (Law 05/2012); no charitable income-tax exemption - NPO income faces 10% profit tax.

Legal personality is automatic by declaration at the prefecture under the 1901 French law; no automatic charitable tax exemption - income taxed under the CGI; 'reconnaissance d'utilite publique' is separate.
